### 3. What Needs to Be Established Before Development Begins

Before you and your teammates start coding, agree on these basics so everyone's pages fit together cleanly without breaking each other's work:

1. **Git Hygiene (`.gitignore` & Branch Rules):**
   - Add a `.gitignore` file to ignore `.DS_Store` (and editor folders like `.vscode/`) so nobody accidentally commits system files.
   - Keep working on your own branch (`i263255` or feature branches off it) and never push directly to `main` until the team reviews/merges changes.

2. **Exact Page Filenames & Navigation Links:**
   - Decide the exact file names for every page (for example: `index.html`, `login.html`, `quiz.html`, `reviews-faq.html`, `packages.html`) so your teammate's navbar/footer links and your quiz's *"View Package"* button point to the right URLs.

3. **How the Shared Header & Footer Will Be Added:**
   - Plain HTML does not automatically reuse a header/footer across multiple pages. Your team should agree on one approach:
     - **Option A (Easiest for beginners / works even if you open files directly by double-clicking):** A shared JavaScript file (e.g., `js/layout.js`) that inserts the header and footer HTML into `<div id="header-placeholder"></div>` and `<div id="footer-placeholder"></div>` on every page.
     - **Option B (`fetch()` partial HTML files):** Loading `components/header.html` via JavaScript `fetch()`. *(Note: this requires running a local server like VS Code **Live Server**, because browsers block `fetch()` on `file://` URLs.)*
   - Until your teammate finishes the real header and footer, your pages should just leave empty placeholder tags (e.g., `<div id="site-header"></div>` and `<div id="site-footer"></div>`) or a simple temporary link bar so you can easily plug their code in later.

4. **Shared Styling & Bootstrap Version:**
   - Confirm which Bootstrap version you are using (e.g., **Bootstrap 5.3** via CDN) and agree on a shared theme palette (brand colors, fonts, button styles) in one global stylesheet (e.g., `css/styles.css`) using CSS variables (`--hh-primary`, etc.).
   - Keep **page-specific CSS and JS in separate files per person/page** so two teammates don't edit the exact same lines and cause Git merge conflicts.

5. **Mock Data & Client-Side Behavior (No Backend Yet):**
   - Since only HTML, CSS, vanilla JS, and Bootstrap are used:
     - Decide what happens when a user logs in/signs up (e.g., form validation + saving a demo session in `localStorage`).
     - Agree on basic package names/IDs so your **Find Your Trip** quiz results match the actual northern Pakistan/Highland trip destinations your teammates create.
     - Decide whether submitted reviews on the **Reviews & FAQ** page save temporarily in `localStorage` so new reviews stay visible on refresh.

6. **Mobile-First & Desktop Layout:**
   - Your paper sketches show mobile screens (`~375px` wide). Using Bootstrap's grid (`container`, `row`, `col-md-*`) will make sure those same screens also look balanced on laptops and desktops.

---

### 4. Suggested Clean Project Structure

For a beginner-friendly HTML/CSS/vanilla JS + Bootstrap project, keeping all `.html` files in the root (or in `pages/`) works well. Keeping `.html` files in the **root folder** is slightly easier for first-semester teams because every page uses the exact same relative paths (like `css/styles.css` or `assets/images/...`) without worrying about `../`.

Here is a clean structure you can propose to your team:

```text
Highland-Horizons/
├── .gitignore                  # Ignores .DS_Store, .vscode/, etc.
├── README.md                   # Project overview, team roles, how to run locally
├── index.html                  # Home page (owned by another teammate)
├── login.html                  # YOUR PAGE: Login / Signup
├── quiz.html                   # YOUR PAGE: Find Your Trip quiz
├── reviews-faq.html            # YOUR PAGE: Traveller Reviews & FAQ
│
├── css/
│   ├── styles.css              # Shared team theme (colors, fonts, common buttons)
│   ├── layout.css              # Teammate's shared header & footer styles
│   ├── auth.css                # Your styles for login.html
│   ├── quiz.css                # Your styles for quiz.html
│   └── reviews-faq.css         # Your styles for reviews-faq.html
│
├── js/
│   ├── layout.js               # Teammate's shared header/footer injection & navbar logic
│   ├── auth.js                 # Your validation & Login/Signup toggle logic
│   ├── quiz.js                 # Your quiz questions, scoring, validation & match result
│   └── reviews-faq.js          # Your rating filters, review submission & FAQ logic
│
├── assets/
│   └── images/                 # Trip photos, logos, icons used on the site
│
└── docs/
    └── prototype-photos/       # Existing paper prototype photos
```

**Why this structure works well for a group project:**
- **Avoids Git conflicts:** Your CSS (`auth.css`, `quiz.css`, `reviews-faq.css`) and JS (`auth.js`, `quiz.js`, `reviews-faq.js`) live in your own files, separate from your teammate's `layout.css` and `layout.js`.
- **Easy to wire up later:** Once your teammate creates `layout.css` and `layout.js`, you only need to include those two files on your three HTML pages.
- **No build tools needed:** Everyone can open and test the site using VS Code's Live Server extension (or directly in a browser).
